title: route-sampler: staged route verification and numeric stepdown for safe alternate-kernel rollout
author: Riya Kapoor

description: Motivation: We need a conservative way to introduce alternate execution routes (new kernels, quantization modes, scheduling heuristics) into production without risking correctness regressions or SLO violations. Prior approaches toggled whole-worker fast/slow modes which caused occasional bit-rot and tail regressions. This change introduces a route-sampler and a numeric-stepdown helper that together allow safe, measurable rollouts.
detailed_description: This PR implements a staged verification and slow ramp for alternate execution routes. Key ideas: 1) Route sampler: a runtime component that probabilistically routes a small percentage of requests to candidate execution routes and records per-request end-to-end correctness signals (hash of deterministic outputs where applicable, divergence heuristics for non-deterministic outputs) and latency distributions. 2) Staged verification: metrics are evaluated on rolling windows; routes that maintain correctness thresholds and meet latency/regression budgets advance through stages (probe -> warmed -> promoted). 3) Numeric stepdown: a lightweight numeric width stepping library that lets us progressively reduce numeric fidelity (e.g., layer-wise reduced-precision warmup) instead of an immediate snap to a lower precision. This reduces catastrophic degradations and provides meaningful intermediate telemetry. 4) Scheduler integration: the scheduler selector consults verified-route metadata to prefer promoted routes for low-latency classes while keeping fallback routes as a safety net. 5) Rollout tooling: runbook and CI benchmark to validate behavior in canary before global promotion.

benchmark_summary: Canary perf runs (internal runner) comparing baseline vs candidate route (with numeric stepdown): median token latency +2%, p95 +6% at 1% sample rate; after warmed promotion median +0.5%, p95 +1.8%. CPU/GPU utilization improved 7% under heavy batching for candidate kernels. No deterministic mismatches observed on deterministic test corpus (15k samples).
safety_and_metrics: Correctness signal: deterministic-hash match or divergence score for stochastic outputs. Promoted only when mismatch rate < 0.01% and p95 regression < 5% over a 30m rolling window. Automatic demotion if error budget or latency budget is exceeded. All promotion events are recorded and surfaced via console. Default sampling rate is 0.5% (configurable per-tenant).
testing: Unit tests cover state transitions and numeric stepdown math paths; integration test simulates scheduler behavior under mixed routes; perf benchmark job runs in CI with synthetic load. Manual canary: staged rollout using the runbook in docs/ops/runbooks/route-sampler.md deployed to a small subset of Dedicated capacity.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: underpowered sampling may miss rare correctness regressions. Mitigation: pipeline to run offline corpus replays against candidate routes and stricter thresholds for deterministic-only workloads. Risk: added complexity in scheduler decisions. Mitigation: fallback routes remain default for high-risk workloads and promotion metadata can be reset via API.
rollout_plan: 1) Enable sampler at 0.5% on canary fleet. 2) Observe metrics for 24h; if thresholds met, ramp to 5% and enable numeric stepdown warming. 3) After 72h stable, promote to 25% then global. Each step can be reverted automatically if thresholds exceeded.

release_notes: Introduce a conservative route-sampler and numeric stepdown mechanism to safely validate and roll out alternate kernels and scheduling heuristics. Enables staged promotion based on correctness and latency budgets; configurable sampling and per-model selectors. No behavioral changes to default routes until promoted.
notes: This is intentionally conservative: all promoted changes require both correctness and latency budgets to be satisfied. Follow-on work: expand deterministic offline replay CLI and refine divergence scoring for chats/multi-turn workloads.
